newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - NEW YORK TIMES FRONT PAGE - AUG 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - NEW YORK TIMES FRONT PAGE - AUG 12.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Tuesday.
* President Clinton used the federal line-item veto to strike down two narrow tax breaks and a provision from the recently signed balanced-budget and tax-cut laws.
* The IMF offered Thailand a $16.0 billion bailout of the country's troubled financial system.
* In using the line-item veto, President Clinton struck down a budget insertion to help New York State finance health care for the poor.
* The Environmental Protection Agency is pushing an emissions-profiles plan that would allow easy on-line acces to data about the polution given off by factories.
* Publishing executives are increasingly turning to book-store chains for guidance about a broad range of issues that could determine how well a book sells.
* United Parcel Service of America Inc ' Teamsters union says its main goal during the strike is to win part-time employees full-time jobs that pay well enough to live on.

* Senate Republicans investigating possible campaign finance abuses are criticizing a 1996 White House luncheon that led to a $100,000 contribution to the Democratic National Committee by the Cheyenne-Arapaho tribe.
